summary: Wataru Mori studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1947 to 1951, working in philosophy and other fields. He held posts at Tokyo Medical and Dental University (circa 1968–1973) and the University of Tokyo (circa 1973–1989).
Wataru S. Ryose is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987. Ryose studied under Minoru Kiyota, Genjun Sasaki, and Frances A. Wilson.

Wayne Proudfoot, a scholar of philosophy and religious studies, studied at Harvard Divinity School and Harvard University (Ph.D. circa 1972). He taught at Fordham University (circa 1970–1972) and served as Professor of Religion at Columbia University (circa 1972–2017).

Wei Lin studied at Nanjing University, Peking University, and Ohio State University (Ph.D. attested 2007) under John C. Huntington. Working in archaeology and Buddhist studies, Lin held posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum, Western Michigan University, and Transylvania University.
Wei Pachow is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology who studied under Tan Yun-shan. He held a teaching and research post at Visva-Bharati University.

Wei-Cheng Lin works in history and archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Lin served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill until 2015 before taking a post at the University of Chicago in 2015.

Weijen Teng studied at the University of Chicago and earned a Ph.D. at Harvard University, supervised by Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil. Working in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy, Teng joined the Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.

Weijue Shi was a Buddhist studies and religious figure who studied under Lingshuan and was ordained under Lingyuan around 1963. He founded the Lin Quan Temple (1987), Chung Tai Shan, and the Chung Tai Buddhist Institute (1993).
Weirong Shen is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held teaching posts at The University of Hong Kong and Renmin University of China (circa 2006–2016).
Weiru Guan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University (attested 2011) under the supervision of Yongdong Shi.
Wen-ling Jane works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Jane earned a Ph.D. at Columbia University, studying under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and teacher Geshe Lozang Jamspal.

Wenbiao Mai studied at Kyoto University, the University of Hamburg, and Peking University, where they earned a Ph.D. Working in Indology and linguistics, Mai held a post at The University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Wendi L. Adamek earned a Ph.D. from Stanford University in 1998, working in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. Adamek held posts at Barnard College (attested 2008) and the University of Calgary (attested 2018).

Wendy Doniger earned doctorates from Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Oxford under Robert Charles Zaehner. A scholar of Indology, religions, and history, she was a professor at the University of Chicago and its Divinity School from 1978 to 2018.

Wenjie Duan studied at Sichuan Fine Arts Institute and the Central Academy of Fine Arts, working in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held multiple leadership roles at Dunhuang Academy from 1946 through 1998, including Director in 1991.
Wenjie Qin is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned a Ph.D. at Harvard University under the supervision of Tu Weiming.

Linguist Werner Abraham studied at TU Wien, Innsbruck, and the University of Vienna (Ph.D. circa 1965). He held posts at Illinois, Tübingen, Groningen (chair from 1971), Munich (2002), and visiting professorships at Cologne, Vienna (2001), and Lund.

Werner Sundermann was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (circa 1970–1991), Humboldt University (circa 1971–1993), and the Free University of Berlin (circa 1993–2000).
Wes Borton is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at East Carolina University under Derek F. Maher and later at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

Whalen Lai studied at International Christian University and Harvard University (Ph.D. circa 1975). In religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, he taught at the University of Illinois (circa 1976–1979) and the University of California, Davis (circa 1979–2009).
